summary:
Phase 3 is still at the survey stage: nothing is implemented yet. This step mapped every source in the work order's §3.1 to the code at vmaf/phase-3 (75cf6e0), separately for mirage_vmaf and for the player, in sources.md. Every number in it comes from a cited file:line, an FFmpeg 8.1.1 source URL, or one of 20 saved runs.

- **The time key exists.** The ladder report already keys every frame to the reference variant's timeline (ref_index and ref_pts), so that timeline is in place.
- **Nothing else feeds it in mirage_vmaf.** It reads only the master playlist. It parses no media playlist, FFmpeg's hls demuxer skips every timeline tag, it records no network timing, and it records no per-frame decoder events. The parsers and the network logger that do exist are built only into the player and the tests.
- **Mapping frames to segments works on a test fixture.** Using each packet's byte position against the segments' sizes named the right segment for all 40 packets. Using timestamps against the playlist's segment durations was wrong at segment boundaries.
- **HTTP timing in mirage_vmaf is not network timing.** It can record when each segment's request started, when its headers arrived, when it was closed and how many bytes were read. But reads are paced by decoding and scoring, so the close time does not measure the download. The HTTP status code is available only through FFmpeg's process-wide log callback.
- **The player has no automatic bitrate switching.** Manual variant switches leave only free-text log lines, and none of them names the rung switched from or to.

sources.md also lists the gaps, the differences from the work order, and 10 design choices with their trade-offs. Each recommendation there is labelled as the agent's; none is a decision. The worktree was not modified.
key_findings: (a) How a ladder report keys a frame: by the pair's own counter, 'index'. Each frame entry also carries ref_index and dis_index, ref_pts and dis_pts, and vmaf. The two PTS are raw seconds: best_effort_timestamp times the stream's time base, not shifted by the input's start. Frames that failed to pair are only in alignment.failures, with input, index, pts and reason. Evidence: <repo>/src/VMAFReport.cpp:193-201, <repo>/src/VMAFAnalyzer.cpp:731-736; run mirage-vmaf-ladder (frame 0 has ref_pts 0.04 and alignment.reference.start 0.04, time_base 1/90000).

(a) No frame is mapped to a segment today. mirage_vmaf compiles neither HlsAlign nor ManifestParser and reads only the master playlist. hls::MediaTimeline (seq, uri, range, start, duration, disc_seq, pdt) is pure code and could be added to it. Evidence: <repo>/CMakeLists.txt:233-246, <repo>/src/VMAFLadder.cpp:293-334, <repo>/src/HlsAlign.h:33-75.

(a) Three ways of naming a packet's segment, tried on the fixture. Byte position (AVPacket::pos against the cumulative bytes_read of the segments SegmentWatch sees): 40 of 40. Timestamp against EXTINF sums: 37 of 40 in plain floating point, 39 of 40 with a half-frame tolerance, because the muxer's last EXTINF is 0.36 s for 10 frames. Open order is unusable: the playlist and three segments were opened before the first packet came back. Evidence: runs map-frames-to-segments, logprobe-file, fixture.

(b) SegmentWatch sees every file opened, the playlist included: the URL, a ' (from byte N)' suffix for a byte range, the return code, and at close bytes_read and error. It keeps only the first file lost, and no time, bytes or status. Evidence: <repo>/src/VMAFSegments.h:59-147; runs logprobe-file and logprobe-http.

(b) NetworkLogger in a process that reads as the analyzer does. Over HTTP it gave the playlist and every segment with status 200, t_sent, t_first_byte and t_end, but bytes -1 (Content-Length only), initiator 'other' and conn_id 0. A local input gave no row. With its own hook instead of SegmentWatch, it also got bytes and connection setup. Evidence: run netlog-probe; <repo>/src/NetworkLogger.cpp:208-235,543-755.

(b) The HTTP status comes only from av_log lines: header='HTTP/…' (TRACE, http.c:1454) or http_code= (TRACE, http.c:1250). Otherwise only a failed open's AVERROR_HTTP_* code gives it (http.c:592-608). No AVOption exports it in 8.1.1 (http.c:180-206). http.c logs 'Latency: avg, max' at close (http.c:2081). The analyzer's reads are paced by scoring, so close time is not network completion. Evidence: run logprobe-http; https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/n8.1.1/libavformat/http.c.

(c) FFmpeg 8.1.1's hls demuxer parses none of DISCONTINUITY, PROGRAM-DATE-TIME, CUE-OUT/CUE-IN, DATERANGE, OATCLS or vendor tags; each is skipped with a VERBOSE 'Skip (...)' line. Over continuous timestamps, two DISCONTINUITY tags gave mirage_vmaf 0 discontinuities. Evidence: hls.c#L989-L991; run logprobe-file (11 Skip lines); run mirage-vmaf-pair-tagged.

(c) ManifestParser's defects:
- CUE-OUT-CONT is classified as CueOut.
- #EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35 is dropped.
- DATERANGE becomes 'Unknown', raw text with SCTE-35 undecoded.
- disc_seq is not incremented at DISCONTINUITY.
- Its 'pts' is playlist time (the sum of EXTINF), not media time.
The player compares these tag times directly with stream PTS. Evidence: <repo>/src/ManifestParser.cpp:302-344; run manifest-probe-tagged; <repo>/src/main.cpp:2888-2914; <repo>/src/NetInspector.cpp:1179-1190.

(d) mirage_vmaf records no per-frame decoder events, and it ignores avcodec_send_packet's return value. On a damaged segment, 6 frames carried decode_error_flags=4 and the decoder printed 17 errors. mirage_vmaf wrote a complete report with a VMAF minimum of 0 and no error field. Key flags and picture types can be read at the same place PTS is recorded (5 I, 9 P, 26 B in the GOP fixture). Frames a decoder drops show only as pairing failures. Evidence: <repo>/src/VMAFAnalyzer.cpp:197-241; runs logprobe-corrupt, mirage-vmaf-pair-corrupt, logprobe-gop.

(e) Variant switches in the player are manual only: request_video_switch has one caller. Every step is logged as free text with logger::uptime() seconds and none names the rung. The media take-over point is the demuxer's 'resume' value. Frames decoded and dropped before the take-over are counted nowhere, though D-068's limits rely on them. Evidence: <repo>/src/main.cpp:1541-1567,1688-1699; <repo>/src/Demuxer.cpp:311-342; <repo>/src/MediaSession.cpp:65-83; run grep-checks.

(f) Process-global state:
- FFmpeg's av_log callback and level are one per process. In a two-thread run, one thread replacing the callback redirected the other thread's lines.
- NetworkLogger is one instance per process, with process-global saved io_open/io_close2.
- SegmentWatch and NetworkLogger's hook both use AVFormatContext::opaque, so they cannot share a context as written.
- logger::uptime() and NetworkLogger::now_us() use different epochs.
Evidence: log.c#L441, #L492; run logprobe-concurrent; <repo>/src/NetworkLogger.cpp:23,244-245,307,351; <repo>/src/VMAFSegments.h:100.

Two more facts for the design:
- The linked libavformat has a dash demuxer, but mirage_vmaf's ladder reads HLS masters only (run demuxers; <repo>/src/VMAFLadder.h:15-22).
- In top-rung mode the top rung is not scored, so a D-068 session that plays it has no score over those spans (<repo>/src/VMAFLadder.h:36-38).
open_issues: D-068 does not say where a scripted test session's per-segment HTTP timing comes from: the plan itself, a separate fetch, or the scoring reads (which scoring paces). The work order's 'segment that took 2.3 seconds' example needs one of them. For the owner.
MEASUREMENT PENDING: whether byte-position mapping of frames to segments holds for fMP4 with EXT-X-MAP, for ID3-timestamped audio and on real D-011 ladders. It was checked only on MPEG-TS.
MEASUREMENT PENDING: whether ref_index and ref_pts of the same reference frame are identical across the pairs of one ladder run.
MEASUREMENT PENDING: whether the player (variant opened through the master) and mirage_vmaf (variant opened alone) give the same PTS for the same frame, including MPEG-TS's 33-bit clock wrap.
decode_error_flags was seen only from FFmpeg's MPEG-2 decoder. What H.264 and HEVC set, AV_FRAME_FLAG_CORRUPT, and frames a decoder never outputs are not measured.
SCTE-35 inside MPEG-TS segments is still unverified, as D-070 says. It was not probed here.
Owner's call: whether logging-only hooks in switch_video, read_loop, video_decode_loop and on_present count as changing the render and decode path under D-007.
Owner's call: how to show the top rung in top-rung-mode sessions, since it is the reference and has no score.

Differences from the work order to report:
- 'NetworkDebugger' is NetworkLogger, and it is built into the player and mirage_tests only.
- There is no ABR.
- Decoder events are not recorded per frame.
- Timeline tags reach no headless code.

FFmpeg's hls muxer, as the fixture used it, wrote TARGETDURATION:0 and a last EXTINF shorter than its frames. D-069's test fixtures should control or check their playlists if tag placement by EXTINF is tested.
<repo>/docs/VMAF_GAP_REPORT.md:230-231 says the Decoder has a dropped-frame counter. The counter is actually the render loop's total_dropped (<repo>/src/main.cpp:1751). Noted, not edited.

The output directory is shared with other workers (schema.md, ui.md, scte35_*, testgen/, schema-survey/, experiments/). Those were not touched. The FFmpeg and RFC source copies were removed because upstream files contain author email addresses; the FETCHED.txt files keep the fetch commands and SHA-256s, and run check-scte35-fixture needs the RFC fetched again to be rerun.
